pairs: Fuit eo tempore vir quidam de monte Ephraim nomine Michas,
In that time, there was a certain man, from mount Ephraim, named Micah.
And he said to his mother,
“The one thousand one hundred silver coins,
which you had separated for yourself,
and about which you had sworn in my hearing,
et super quibus me audiente juraveras,
“My son has been blessed by the Lord.”
Therefore, he restored them to his mother.
Consecravi et vovi hoc argentum Domino,
“I have consecrated and vowed this silver to the Lord,
ut de manu mea suscipiat filius meus,
so that my son would receive it from my hand,
and would make a molten idol and a graven image.
And now I deliver it to you.”
And when he restored these to his mother,
she took two hundred of the silver coins,
and she gave them to the silversmith,
ut faceret ex eis sculptile atque conflatile,
so that he might make from them a molten idol and a graven image.
And it was in the house of Micah.
Qui ædiculam quoque in ea deo separavit,
And he also separated in it a little shrine for the god.
And he filled the hand of one of his sons,
In diebus illis non erat rex in Israël,
In those days, there was no king in Israel.
sed unusquisque quod sibi rectum videbatur, hoc faciebat.
Instead, each one did what seemed right to himself.
Fuit quoque alter adolescens de Bethlehem Juda,
Also, there was another young man, from Bethlehem of Judah,
And he himself was a Levite,
Then, departing from the city of Bethlehem,
peregrinari voluit ubicumque sibi commodum reperisset.
he wished to sojourn wherever he would find it beneficial to himself.
Cumque venisset in montem Ephraim, iter faciens,
And when he had arrived at mount Ephraim, while making the journey,
et declinasset parumper in domum Michæ,
he also turned aside for a little while to the house of Micah.
interrogatus est ab eo unde venisset.
And he was asked by him where he came from.
“I am a Levite from Bethlehem of Judah.
et vado ut habitem ubi potuero,
And I am traveling so that I may live where I am able,
if I perceive it to be useful to me.”
et esto mihi parens ac sacerdos:
And you shall be to me like a parent and a priest.
daboque tibi per annos singulos decem argenteos,
And I will give to you, each year, ten silver coins,
et quæ ad victum sunt necessaria.
and he stayed with the man.
fuitque illi quasi unus de filiis.
And he was to him like one of his sons.
et habuit puerum sacerdotem apud se:
and he had the young man with him as his priest,
“Now I know that God will be good to me,
quod benefaciet mihi Deus habenti Levitici generis sacerdotem.
since I have a priest from the stock of the Levites.”
